title: Skill Development Programmes for Tribals
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Tribal Affairs Skill Development Programmes for Tribals प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 2:13PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed today in Lok Sabha that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs implements the scheme Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM) and Pradhan Mantri Janjati Maha Nyaya Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) through Tribal Co-operative Marketing Development Federation (TRIFED) to facilitate and promote livelihood opportunities and entrepreneurship in the tribal population through establishment of Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs). Under PMJVM scheme, 4,172 VDVKs, covering 12.48 lakh beneficiaries have been sanctioned in 28 States/UTs, with a total sanctioned amount of ₹619.17 crore. While under PM-JANMAN scheme, 540 VDVKs, covering 0.46 lakh beneficiaries have been sanctioned in 18 states/UTs, with a total sanctioned amount of ₹23.02 crore. During the last three financial years (2023-24 to 2025-26), 617 VDVKs have been sanctioned under PMJVM and 540 VDVKs under PM JANMAN across various States/ UTs. Through these VDVKs, support has been provided for skill development, capacity building, value addition, processing, plantation, and marketing assistance, alongside the creation of self-employment opportunities and livelihood enhancement. Additionally, National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC), a Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE), provides concessional loans to the eligible Scheduled Tribe persons for undertaking income generation, self-employment and livelihood activities. In the last five years, NSTFDC has disbursed loans amounting to ₹1648.39 cr to 4,95,090 ST beneficiaries under its various schemes. title: RECRUITMENT OF TEACHERS AND STAFF IN EMRSs
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Tribal Affairs RECRUITMENT OF TEACHERS AND STAFF IN EMRSs प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 2:12PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed today in Lok Sabha that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs has not received any representations to reverse the centralized recruitment process for teachers and staff in Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs). The Government has sanctioned 31 teaching posts and 21 non-teaching posts per EMRS for EMRSs with classes up to 12th having a full strength of 480 students to be recruited in phased manner. 13 of the 21 non-teaching posts sanctioned for each school have been earmarked for engagement through outsourcing, with the objective of promoting local employment and community participation. Centralized recruitment mechanism through the EMRS Staff Selection Examination (ESSE) has been instituted to ensure the appointment of qualified and competent teaching and non-teaching personnel across EMRSs. 9111 teaching & non -teaching staff have already been recruited and examination has been conducted for another batch of 7267 teaching & non -teaching staff for EMRSs across the country. Staff who have joined in EMRSs are provided with training in different areas including importance of Tribal culture, ways to improve the standard of the tribal students and learning regional languages. To familiarise with the Tribal culture, language and local requirement arrangement is made to have sessions on local languages through State educational Societies and also through regional language teachers who are posted in EMRSs. As per the terms and conditions of offer of appointment, candidates are also required to qualify the regional language competency requirement of the State in which posting is done during the probation period. title: STATUS OF EMRSs IN WEST BENGAL
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Tribal Affairs STATUS OF EMRSs IN WEST BENGAL प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 2:10PM by PIB Delhi The Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri. Durgadas Uikey informed today in Lok Sabha that the  Ministry of Tribal Affairs is implementing the scheme of Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS) for providing quality education to tribal students in their own environment preserving local art and culture. EMRS are established in tribal dominated blocks having more than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons, as per Census 2011. As on date, 728 EMRSs have been approved out of which 508 are functional across the country. In West Bengal 9 EMRSs have been approved and all are functional. None of the blocks in Alipurduar districts fulfil the prescribed criteria for establishing EMRS. National Education Society for Tribal Students (NESTS) , an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, provides overall policy direction, academic support, monitoring, capacity building, recruitment, standardization of processes and implementation of the EMRS Scheme across the country. State EMRS Societies oversee the implementation, administration and day-to-day management of EMRSs within their jurisdictions. District Level EMRS Committees , under the Chairmanship of the District Collector/District Magistrate s do local oversight and resolve local implementation issues. The status of sanctioned, operational and under construction EMRSs in West Bengal, district wise is given at Annexure. title: DISPLACEMENT OF STs IN TIGER RESERVE AREAS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Tribal Affairs DISPLACEMENT OF STs IN TIGER RESERVE AREAS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 2:06PM by PIB Delhi The Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri. Durgadas Uikey informed today in Lok Sabha that the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) is mandated to inquire into complaints regarding the deprivation of rights and safeguards of the Scheduled Tribes which include issues related to alienation, development, atrocities, forest right claims, etc. including displacement of Scheduled Tribes from Tiger Reserve areas on a case-to-case basis and makes appropriate recommendations to the concerned authorities, wherever warranted. A few representations regarding voluntary village relocation from Tiger Reserves have been forwarded to the NTCA by the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST). It has been clarified that the process of relocation of villages from Core/Critical Tiger Habitats is voluntary as per the provisions of Section 38 V (5) of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 2006, and Section 4(2) of the Forest Rights Act, 2006. The National Tiger Conservation Authority (Normative Standards for Tourism activities and Project Tiger) Guidelines, 2012, issued under section 38 O (1) (c) of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, are also available in the public domain which clearly outline the principle of voluntary relocation which has been reiterated to all State Governments in different forms, from time to time. The implementation of village relocation is undertaken by the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations in accordance with the prescribed guidelines, and District Level Committees are constituted by the concerned States and Union Territories to facilitate effective implementation. The Guidelines issued by this authority provide for a rehabilitation package for voluntary village relocation, including settlement of rights, agricultural land and house construction etc. The framework also provides for provision of basic amenities and convergence with other Government schemes to ensure that relocated families are able to access welfare and development benefits. The financial assistance for voluntary relocation has been enhanced from ₹10 lakh to ₹15 lakh per family in 2021. Insofar as the Ministry of Tribal Affairs is concerned, the State Governments and UT Administrations have been exhorted to ensure that no rightful beneficiary is deprived of their forest rights, including compliance with Section 4(5) of the Forest Rights Act, 2006, which stipulates that the claimants cannot be evicted or removed from forest land under their occupation till the recognition and verification procedure is complete. The National Tiger Conservation Authority has reiterated to all Tiger Range States that village rehabilitation shall be completely voluntary and that informed consent of the Gram Sabha and the concerned people shall be obtained before undertaking rehabilitation. The States have been advised to undertake voluntary village relocation in accordance with the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972, the Forest Rights Act, 2006 and the guidelines issued by this authority. The National Tiger Conservation Authority (Normative Standards for Tourism activities and Project Tiger) Guidelines, 2012, issued under section 38 O (1) (c) of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, are also available in the public domain which clearly outline the principle of voluntary relocation which has been reiterated to all State Governments in different forms, from time to time. Consultations with the Gram Sabha are conducted by the respective State Governments which carry out thorough due diligence which incorporate prior informed consent and voluntariness as enshrined in the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and the Scheduled Tribes and Other Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006. In order to ensure transparency of process, the said guidelines recommend that the relocation process could be monitored and implemented by the two committees namely, State Level Monitoring Committee & District Level Implementing Committee which consists of representatives from tribal welfare department too. Accordingly, an institutional mechanism for monitoring voluntary village relocation is already provided under the existing framework, and the concerned State Governments undertake relocation in accordance with the prescribed statutory provisions and guidelines. It is to be informed that there are no reports of involuntary or coerced relocation reported to this authority by the State-level Monitoring Committees and District-level Implementing Committees, which are mandated to oversee the process. title: “EDUCATION AND HOUSING SCHEMES FOR STS IN KERALA”
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Tribal Affairs “EDUCATION AND HOUSING SCHEMES FOR STS IN KERALA” प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 2:05PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed today in Lok Sabha that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs implements the following five ongoing scholarship schemes for Scheduled Tribe (ST) students across the country, including the State of Kerala. The annual family income limits prescribed under the guidelines of these schemes are as under: S. No. Name of Scheme Annual Family Income Limit 1 Pre-Matric Scholarship for ST students (Class IX and X) Rs. 2.50 lakhs 2 Post Matric Scholarship for ST students (Class XI and above) Rs. 2.50 lakhs 3 National Scholarship for Higher Education for ST students (Top Class) Rs. 6.00 lakhs 4 National Fellowship for Higher Education for ST students (NFST) No Income Limit 5 National Overseas Scholarship for ST students (NOS) Rs. 6.00 lakhs Apart from this, 'National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC), under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, an apex organisation set up exclusively for economic development of Scheduled Tribes, extends concessional loans to the eligible Scheduled Tribe persons for undertaking any income generation activities/ self-employment including education loan through its implementing agencies across the country including the state of Kerala. In case of individuals, having annual family income not exceeding ₹ 3 lakh p.a. both for rural and urban areas are eligible for availing concessional loans under the NSTFDC schemes. In addition to above education support provided by the Central Government, as informed by the State Govt. of Kerala, it is also running its own Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme under which benefit is provided to all eligible ST students without any prescribed criteria of annual family income. The intervention of housing under PM JANMAN scheme of this Ministry is being implemented by Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) through PMAY-G scheme. As per the approved norms, there is no prescribed annual income limit for sanctioning of awas to Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTG) beneficiaries. However, there are only two (02) exclusion criteria in respect of PVTG households – (i) household with pucca houses and (ii) Household with any member as a government employee. Further, housing assistance is also provided by the State Govt. of Kerala through their LIFE Mission. As per the guidelines of the LIFE Mission Scheme, the annual family income ceiling prescribed for availing housing benefits is ₹3.00 lakh. As per the information received from State Govt. of Kerala, the majority of the Scheduled Tribe population in Kerala belongs to the economically weaker sections. It has not come to the notice of the State Government that a large number of Scheduled Tribe beneficiaries are being excluded from housing schemes on account of the prescribed income limit. In cases where Scheduled Tribe families are not eligible for housing assistance under the LIFE Mission due to prescribed income ceiling, they may be considered for housing assistance under the housing schemes implemented by the Scheduled Tribes Development Department, Govt. of Kerala. With regard to educational assistance, the question does not arise since there is no prescribed annual family income in the State Govt. of Kerala. The appraisal and approval of the Expenditure Finance Commission (EFC) for their continuation of schemes implemented by M/o Tribal Affairs during F.Y. 2026-27 to 2030-31 is currently ongoing wherein, inter-alia, the proposal to revise the annual family income ceiling is included for seeking the approval of the Dept. of Expenditure on the draft EFC. The decision regarding enhancing the annual income limit under the said schemes in the EFC is subject to the approval of the Competent Authority. title: Implementation of Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Tribal Affairs Implementation of Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 2:00PM by PIB Delhi The Union Minister of Tribal Affairs Shri Jual Oram today laid a statement on the Table of the House that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs has reviewed the implementation of Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan on a continuous basis through periodic monitoring at the Ministry, State and district levels. The review has noted that Phase-I has established a nationwide community-based capacity-building framework for strengthening last-mile governance in tribal areas. The programme aims to create a cadre of trained government functionaries, community leaders, women’s collectives and tribal youth to facilitate responsive governance across approximately one lakh tribal villages in 30 States/UTs. The programme has made significant progress towards developing transformative tribal leadership by creating a large cadre of trained grassroots leaders drawn from government institutions as well as tribal communities. The achievement made in developing transformative Tribal leadership through the abhiyan during phase 1 is as follow: Approx. 15 lakh Adi Karmayogis mobilised through a cascading training architecture. More than 210 State Master Trainers, 2,200+ District Master Trainers and 11,000+ Block Master Trainers developed. 6,79,309 Adi Saathis and 4,03,306 Adi Sahyogis mobilised. 62,187 Tribal Village Vision 2030 Plans approved through Gram Sabhas. 54,324 Village Workbooks and 56,422 Adi Sewa Kendras (ASKs) recorded under the programme. The Ministry has established an institutional mechanism to ensure continuity of capacity building, mentoring and follow-up support through Adi Sewa Kendras (ASKs) and Adi Karmayogi Volunteers (AKVs) . The programme strengthens community leadership and participatory development by placing Gram Sabhas and tribal communities at the centre of local planning and implementation. During Phase-I, communities undertook household surveys, transect walks, focus group discussions and development-gap assessments, culminating in preparation of Tribal Village Vision 2030 documents and Village Action Plans covering health, education, livelihoods, housing, drinking water, connectivity, financial inclusion and social protection. Gram Sabhas formally approved these plans, thereby institutionalising participatory decision-making. Under this mechanism, the following mechanism is contributing to strengthening community leadership and participatory development in tribal areas: Adi Sewa Kendras (ASK) function as village-level single-window facilitation centres for information dissemination, entitlement facilitation, grievance redressal support and convergence with line departments. title: STATUS OF VAN DHAN VIKAS KENDRA CLUSTERS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Tribal Affairs STATUS OF VAN DHAN VIKAS KENDRA CLUSTERS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 1:56PM by PIB Delhi The Union Minister of Tribal Affairs Shri Jual Oram today laid a statement on the Table of the House that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs provides financial support for establishment of Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs) through Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India Limited (TRIFED) under the Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM) and Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN). As on date 4,712 VDVKs, covering 12.94 lakh beneficiaries, have been sanctioned in 28 States/UTs, with a total sanctioned amount of Rs. 642.19 crore under both the schemes out of which 3,406 VDVKs are operational. A maximum amount of Rs 15.00 lakhs is provided to State Governments to set up one VDVK for incurring the expenditure on raw material, training and capacity building, tool kits and machinery, mentoring charges, packaging and branding, transportation, storage etc. Revolving working capital is not provided to VDVKs under the schemes. However, under the Minimum Support Price (MSP) component of the scheme, revolving fund is provided to State Implementing Agencies (SIAs) for undertaking Minor Forest Produce (MFP) procurement from tribal MFP gatherers at MSP, in case the market price falls below the MSP. During the Financial Year 2025–26, an amount of Rs. 2.50 crore has been released to the State Implementing Agency (SIA) of Meghalaya for the procurement of MFP. Fund release for establishment of VDVKs is undertaken through Treasury Single Account (TSA) system introduced by Ministry of Finance. TSA accounts have been opened by almost all State Implementing Agencies, and funds are being transferred to the TSA accounts of the SIAs. TSA system provides the treasury and central bank total oversight over liquidity, eliminates idle cash parked in commercial banks, and ensures "just-in-time" release of funds for public expenditures. As mentioned in reply to part (a) above, revolving working capital is not provided to VDVKs under PMJVM / PM-JANMAN schemes. Operational VDVKs are encouraged to graduate into Van Dhan Producer Enterprises (VDPEs) for value addition, aggregation and market linkage based on their performance. One VDPE proposal from the State of Madhya Pradesh has been approved in principle for implementation. A total of 148 VDVKs are operational in the state of Chhattisgarh under the PM-JANMAN and PMJVM Schemes. Revolving funds amounting to ₹153.66 crores have been released to Chhattisgarh SIA for procurement of MFPs since 2013-14 through which MFPs worth ₹467 crores have been procured by the State till 2025-26. Chhattisgarh SIA has submitted the claim for reimbursement of losses under the MSP operations which is under examination. No proposal for procurement of MFPs has been received from the State of Chhattisgarh during the current financial year. The matter has been discussed with the SIAs, and they have been advised to devise appropriate mechanisms for transferring funds directly to the bank accounts of VDVKs and ground-level primary procurement agencies. In some States, funds are already being transferred directly to the bank accounts of VDVKs. EMRS are established in tribal dominated blocks having more than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons, as per Census 2011. As on date, 728 EMRSs have been approved out of which 508 are functional across the country having 156593 students enrolled during the Academic Session 2025-26. In the State of Telangana 23 EMRSs have been sanctioned and all of them are functional with10199 students enrolled during the Academic Session 2025-26. Various steps have been undertaken to enhance the quality of education and sports facilities in EMRSs across the country such as well-equipped classrooms with modern teaching aids, bridge courses, remedial classes science and computer laboratories, libraries with diverse learning resources, playgrounds and sports equipment, facilities for extracurricular activities like music, art, and sports, smart classrooms for digital education, computer labs with internet access, skill development and vocational training programs on a pparel, Automotive, AR/VR, AI, Beauty & Wellness, Agriculture, Electronics, and retail to enhance employability, etc. The preservation and promotion of tribal culture, language and traditional knowledge are integral to the objective of Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS) Scheme. To achieve this, Tribal Corners have been established in EMRSs to showcase and preserve the culture, traditions, art, crafts and heritage of tribal communities. Cultural Programs, Meets and workshops are organized to provide a platform for students to learn about, appreciate and celebrate the diverse tribal cultures and traditions of the country. title: Semiconductor and AI Revolution
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau PIB Backgrounder Semiconductor and AI Revolution Powering the Future प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 1:47PM by PIB Delhi Powering the Future From Chips to AI: Building India’s Technology Leadership Semiconductors are the foundation of modern technology, powering everything from smartphones and vehicles to satellites and AI systems. AI is now accelerating the demand for advanced chips, specialised processors and high-performance computing, making the two technologies increasingly inseparable. Recognising this convergence, India is building capabilities from chip design and fabrication to computing infrastructure and indigenous AI models. Government initiatives across both sectors are creating an integrated technology ecosystem that strengthens self-reliance, supply-chain resilience and innovation. This convergence is also opening new opportunities in advanced manufacturing, research, entrepreneurship and high-value employment. As India marks its 80th Independence Day , these capabilities mark a decisive step towards global technology leadership and a Viksit Bharat. Semiconductors: Foundation for Technological Self-Reliance India is building domestic capabilities across the semiconductor value chain, from chip design and fabrication to advanced packaging, equipment and materials. By strengthening domestic capabilities today, India is positioning itself to shape the technologies of tomorrow. Dedicated Mission Laid The Foundation For Self-Reliance Semicon 1.0 laid the foundation with a ₹76,000 crore outlay to build India’s semiconductor ecosystem. It supports the entire value chain, spanning chip design, fabrication, packaging, testing, equipment, materials and skilled talent etc. Semicon 2.0 is scaling this foundation into global ecosystem leadership, with a ₹1,27,500 crore outlay approved in July 2026. Six strategic pillars drive Semicon India 2.0: chip design, semiconductor equipment and materials, fabrication facilities, advanced packaging, research and development, and talent development. This integrated approach strengthens supply-chain resilience, expands domestic value addition and positions India for future semiconductor leadership. From Policy to Semiconductor Manufacturing 12 semiconductor projects have been approved across six states , with investments commitments exceeding ₹ 1.64 lakh crore . Projects span silicon and compound semiconductor fabs, display fabrication and advanced packaging facilities. Three facilities have already commenced commercial production, marking India’s transition from semiconductor policy to manufacturing. Semiconductor facilities will supply critical components for automobiles, telecommunications, aerospace, power electronics and consumer electronics Semiconductor fabs plants that build raw silicon wafers into functioning integrated circuits and microchips. Display fabrication are Plants that build flat and flexible screens for phones, cars, and gadgets etc. Advanced packaging methods that encase, wire, and shield fragile chips to make them run faster and last longer. Developing Indigenous Semiconductor Design Capabilities To meet future workforce requirements, the Government has prioritised semiconductor skilling through initiatives such as Chips to Startup (C2S), under which, Electronic Design Automation ( EDA) tools have been deployed in 320 academic institutions and Over 68,000 students trained, expanding access to advanced chip-design capabilities. Click to Read More About: Chips to Start-up (C2S) Programme 24 semiconductor design projects have also been approved for financial support and 105 startups/MSMEs for EDA tool support under DLI Scheme . title: Empowering Youth, Transforming India
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau PIB Backgrounder Empowering Youth, Transforming India प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 1:18PM by PIB Delhi Amrit Peedhi for Viksit Bharat@2047 India is home to one of the world’s largest youth populations, with nearly 65 percent of its citizens below the age of 35. Over the years, the Government has expanded investment across education, skilling, employment, entrepreneurship, sports, health, and civic participation to convert this demographic advantage into a development dividend. Together, these efforts are enabling the Amrit Peedhi to shape Viksit Bharat @ 2047. MY Bharat: A Platform for Youth-Led Development At the centre of this vision is Mera Yuva Bharat, launched in October 2023 for youth aged 15–29. The technology-enabled platform brings volunteering, experiential learning, leadership, skilling, career support and civic participation into a single nationwide ecosystem. Growing national platform – More than 2.22 crore youth have registered on the platform for volunteering, experiential learning, leadership, skilling, and career opportunities, as of July 2026. Volunteering at scale – Over 1.52 lakh volunteering opportunities enable young people to participate in community service, environmental action, cultural initiatives and public programmes. Learning through experience – More than 24,900 experiential learning programmes have connected youth with governance, healthcare, media, technology and public service. Digital Engagement and Civic Participation Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue 2026 – More than 50 lakh youth participated through a nationwide quiz. The dialogue also involved 78 diaspora youth from 21 countries and identified 6,000 young leaders for a district-wise repository. National Service Scheme (NSS) – Volunteer enrolment increased from 34.09 lakh in 2014–15 to 38.90 lakh in 2025–26. Education: Access, Quality and Future-Readiness The education ecosystem has expanded while becoming more flexible, digital and innovation-driven. National Education Policy 2020 places the learner at the centre and links schooling, higher education, skills and employability. One of the world’s largest school systems – India has 14.67 lakh schools serving 24.72 crore students, supported by more than 1.02 crore teachers. Improved retention – The secondary-school dropout rate declined from 14.54 % in 2013–14 to 7 in 2025–26. Digital classrooms – Over 1.49 lakh schools were covered under ICT and digital initiatives by 2025–26, with more than 1.76 lakh smart classrooms and 1.79 lakh ICT laboratories sanctioned (as of March 2026). Atal Tinkering Labs – More than 10,000 labs have engaged over 1.1 crore student innovators and supported more than 16 lakh projects. Higher Education and Innovation Rising enrolment – Higher-education enrolment increased from 3.4 crore in 2014–15 to 4.5 crore in 2023–24; Female enrolment increased 42.2% since 2014-2015 to 2.2 crores in 2023-24. Institutional growth Incubation and research – 85 Atal Incubation Centres have created 32,000+ jobs and supported over 2,900 startups. Flexible Learning and Digital Access National Credit Framework – More than 700 universities and over 7,500 affiliated colleges have adopted the National Credit Framework (NCrF). Academic Bank of Credits – 3,123 institutions have been onboarded and more than 35.27 crore APAAR IDs issued, enabling learners to store, transfer, and redeem credits. (as on 12 th August 2026). SWAYAM – As on 12 th August 2026, the platform offers more than 20,370 courses and has recorded 6.5 crore+ enrolments. DIKSHA – Across India, 342 courses have recorded 19.06 crore enrolments, 15.02 crore completions, and the issuance of 13 crore certificates (as on 12 th August 2026). Skilling and Employability The Government has empowered over 6 crore people through its skilling initiatives. Skill India Mission has shifted training from basic certification towards a demand-led model connected with industry, apprenticeships, digital platforms, and emerging technologies. Lower unemployment – The unemployment rate declined from 7.71 per cent in 2014 to 4.2 per cent in 2025. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) – More than 1.64 crore youth have been trained across four phases since 2015. PMKVY includes industry-linked training in AI, robotics, drones, electronics, green energy, and other future-facing sectors, with on-the-job exposure. Jan Shikshan Sansthan – 36.48 lakh people were trained till March 2026. National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) – More than 54.41 lakh apprentices were engaged till March 2026. Startup India – The number of startups grew from about 350 before 2014 to more than 2.47 lakh by August 2026, making India the world’s third-largest startup ecosystem. Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme - As of 12 th August, 2026, the PM Internship Scheme has provided 1,64, 902 internship opportunities across 31 sectors. PM-SETU – Launched in October 2025 with an estimated outlay of ₹60,000 crore to upgrade 1,000 government ITIs through 200 hubs and 800 spokes, with industry participation and labor-market-led courses. Between 2014 and 2025, ITIs increased from 9,977 to 14,688; enrolment from 9.5 lakh to 14.7 lakh; National Skill Training Institutes from 25 to 33; and Institutes for Training of Trainers from 11 to 120. Sports and Fitness India has built a structured sports pathway that begins with local talent identification and extends to high-performance support. Sport is increasingly seen as a viable career, backed by coaching, infrastructure, scientific training and competition exposure. Khelo India infrastructure – Under the scheme, 349 infrastructure projects worth ₹3,176 crore have been approved, alongside the establishment of 1,067 Khelo India Centres and 267 academies. The scheme also supports 2,745 athletes. Khelo India Games – Since 2018, more than 63,000 athletes have participated in the Youth, University, Winter, Para, Beach, Water Sports and Tribal Games. Support for elite athletes – The Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) supports 51 Core, 52 Para Core and 130 Development athletes. Core and Development athletes receive monthly stipends of ₹50,000 and ₹25,000, respectively. Expanded investment – The revamped Khelo India Scheme and enhanced support for National Sports Federations have a combined outlay of ₹36,441 crore for the period 2026–27 to 2030–31. Health and Well-being Youth empowerment depends on physical, mental, and preventive healthcare. Government programmes have expanded adolescent-friendly services, mental-health counselling, substance-abuse awareness, and access to comprehensive primary care. Adolescent health – Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics (AFHCs) increased from 6,619 in 2014–15 to 7,203 in 2021–22. Adolescents receiving clinical and counselling services rose from 39 lakh to 82 lakh in the same period; 97.67 lakh youth registered in the clinic in 2024–25 up to November 2024. Mental health – Tele-MANAS has handled over 43.70 lakh calls through 53 cells, supported by 23 mentoring institutes and five Regional Coordinating Centres (as on 12 th August 2026). Substance-abuse prevention – As on 12 th August, 2026, Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan has reached over 30.05 crore people , including 11.86 crore youth. More than 28.56 lakh activities have been conducted in educational institutions, while over 28.29 lakh persons have received treatment and rehabilitation support. A Decade of Transformation Twelve years of sustained, multi-sectoral investment have produced a measurable transformation in India’s youth. More young Indians are staying in education, acquiring industry-relevant skills, entering formal employment, creating businesses, participating in community life, and competing at the highest levels of sport. The shift has been from access to opportunity, from participation to leadership, and from youth as beneficiaries to youth as co-creators. Policy, institutions, and digital platforms have laid a strong foundation; the Amrit Peedhi is carrying it forward towards Viksit Bharat @ 2047. Jan Shikshan Sansthan – 36.48 lakh people were trained till March 2026. National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) – More than 54.41 lakh apprentices were engaged till March 2026. Startup India – The number of startups grew from about 350 before 2014 to more than 2.47 lakh by August 2026, making India the world’s third-largest startup ecosystem. Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme - As of 12 th August, 2026, the PM Internship Scheme has provided 1,64, 902 internship opportunities across 31 sectors. PM-SETU – Launched in October 2025 with an estimated outlay of ₹60,000 crore to upgrade 1,000 government ITIs through 200 hubs and 800 spokes, with industry participation and labor-market-led courses. Between 2014 and 2025, ITIs increased from 9,977 to 14,688; enrolment from 9.5 lakh to 14.7 lakh; National Skill Training Institutes from 25 to 33; and Institutes for Training of Trainers from 11 to 120. Sports and Fitness India has built a structured sports pathway that begins with local talent identification and extends to high-performance support. Sport is increasingly seen as a viable career, backed by coaching, infrastructure, scientific training and competition exposure. Khelo India infrastructure – Under the scheme, 349 infrastructure projects worth ₹3,176 crore have been approved, alongside the establishment of 1,067 Khelo India Centres and 267 academies. The scheme also supports 2,745 athletes. Khelo India Games – Since 2018, more than 63,000 athletes have participated in the Youth, University, Winter, Para, Beach, Water Sports and Tribal Games. Support for elite athletes – The Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) supports 51 Core, 52 Para Core and 130 Development athletes. Core and Development athletes receive monthly stipends of ₹50,000 and ₹25,000, respectively. Expanded investment – The revamped Khelo India Scheme and enhanced support for National Sports Federations have a combined outlay of ₹36,441 crore for the period 2026–27 to 2030–31. Health and Well-being Youth empowerment depends on physical, mental, and preventive healthcare. Government programmes have expanded adolescent-friendly services, mental-health counselling, substance-abuse awareness, and access to comprehensive primary care. Adolescent health – Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics (AFHCs) increased from 6,619 in 2014–15 to 7,203 in 2021–22. Adolescents receiving clinical and counselling services rose from 39 lakh to 82 lakh in the same period; 97.67 lakh youth registered in the clinic in 2024–25 up to November 2024. Mental health – Tele-MANAS has handled over 43.70 lakh calls through 53 cells, supported by 23 mentoring institutes and five Regional Coordinating Centres (as on 12 th August 2026). Substance-abuse prevention – As on 12 th August, 2026, Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan has reached over 30.05 crore people , including 11.86 crore youth. More than 28.56 lakh activities have been conducted in educational institutions, while over 28.29 lakh persons have received treatment and rehabilitation support. A Decade of Transformation Twelve years of sustained, multi-sectoral investment have produced a measurable transformation in India’s youth. More young Indians are staying in education, acquiring industry-relevant skills, entering formal employment, creating businesses, participating in community life, and competing at the highest levels of sport. The shift has been from access to opportunity, from participation to leadership, and from youth as beneficiaries to youth as co-creators. Policy, institutions, and digital platforms have laid a strong foundation; the Amrit Peedhi is carrying it forward towards Viksit Bharat @ 2047. title: Expanding the Development Horizon

Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau PIB Backgrounder Expanding the Development Horizon Ensuring Welfare, Inclusion, and Empowerment for Rural and Tribal Communities प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 12:27PM by PIB Delhi India’s development story is reaching deeper into rural and tribal communities, transforming access, opportunity, and quality of life. From basic services and resilient infrastructure to livelihoods, skills, education, and financial security, interventions are expanding the foundations of inclusive growth. Focused efforts for women, tribal communities, and vulnerable groups are further strengthening pathways to dignity and empowerment. These initiatives are reshaping rural India through wider opportunity, stronger communities, and more equitable development. From Welfare Delivery to Decentralised Partnerships Direct fiscal transfers to gram panchayats have been increased. It has been increased from ₹2.36 lakh crore under the 15 th Finance Commission (2021–26) to ₹4.35 lakh crore under the 16 th Finance Commission (2026–31). The Union Budget for rural development has been increased from ₹87,765 crore (2016–17) to ₹2.73 lakh crore (2026–27). The Union Budget for tribal affairs has been increased from ₹4,826 crore (2016–17) to ₹15,421.97 crore (2026–27). Foundations of Dignity: Universal Access to Basic Needs Jal Jeevan Mission Household tap water coverage increased from 3.23 crore (August 2019) to over 15.91 crore (August 12, 2026). As of August 12, 2026, 2.89 lakh villages have reported 100% tap water coverage under Har Ghar Jal campaign. Swachh Bharat Abhiyan - Grameen Over 12.19 crore individual household toilets have been constructed, as of August 12, 2026. India was declared Open Defecation Free in 2019 . Over 1,288 GOBARdhan biogas plants are operational, as of August 11, 2026, compared to 14 plants in FY 2018-19. Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana As of August 12, 2026, over 10.57 crore free LPG connections have been provided to women from below-poverty-line households . The total number of LPG connections in India has increased from 14.52 crore in 2014 to 33.39 crore in 2026. Universal Village Electrification 100% willing household electrification (pan-India level) was achieved by March 2019 under PM Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (SAUBHAGYA) . Under the Deendayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana , 100% village electrification was achieved by 2025 . Ayushman Bharat More than 45.51 crore Ayushman Cards have been issued as of August 12, 2026. 96.43 crore ABHA accounts have been created as of August 12, 2026. Over 1.86 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs are currently functional (as of August 12, 2026). Food Security for All PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana provides free foodgrains to over 81.35 crore beneficiaries. 99.8% Fair Price Shops under the PDS are automated for Aadhaar-based distribution , as of July 29, 2026. Ration cards are 100% digitised across all States/UTs as of July 29, 2026. As of July 29, 2026, over 221 crore portability transactions have been recorded under One Nation One Ration Card . Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan (Sarva Shiksha Abhiyaan) Between 2018-19 to 2025-26, 4,073 schools have been upgraded and 1.49 lakh ICT and digital initiatives implemented. Further, 25,000 schools are covered under skill education . 97.3% of the schools are equipped with functional female sanitation facilities. F emale drop-out rate at primary school level decreased from 4.6% (2013-14) to 0.1% (2025-26). At secondary school level , it reduced from 14.5% (2013-14) to 8% (2025-26). Reservation for Economically Weaker Section and Improved Enrolment Levels 10% EWS reservation provided for candidates outside existing SC, ST, and OBC reservation categories in 2019. This decision benefits the economically disadvantaged individuals from the general category. In 2025-26, Gross Enrollment Ratio (GER) was recorded 89.4 at primary level and 81.5 at secondary level. GER at higher secondary level increased to 61.7 in 2025-26 as compared to 46.4 in 2014-15. Beti Bachao Beti Padhao Girls’ Gross Enrollment Ratio (GER) for girls at the secondary level (Classes 9–10) rose from 75.5% in 2014–15 to 83.4% in 2025–26 . Kasturba Balika Vidyalayas and PM eVidya The number of sanctioned schools increased from 3,609 (2014–15) to 5,639 (2024-25). Operational KGBVs stand at 5,133, as of 2024–25. Enrolment increased from 3.52 lakh (2014–15) to 7.11 lakh (2024). The SWAYAM portal (India’s indigenous MOOC platform) has over 6.5 crore enrolments (as of August 12, 2026). As of August 12, 2026, DIKSHA has 2.35 crore registered users. Building the Backbone: Infrastructure and Connectivity Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana – Grameen Under PMAY-G, over 3.91 crore houses have been sanctioned, and 3.13 crore houses have been completed (as of August 12, 2026). Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana As of June 2026, 99.6% of eligible habitations have been connected with all-weather roads . Completed length of roads increased from 3.86 lakh km (May 2000 – May 2014) to 4.13 lakh km (May 2014 – August 12, 2026). Completed number of bridges rose from 484 to 10,404 during May 2014 – August 12, 2026. Digitalization of Gram Panchayats Under BharatNet , 2.19 lakh Gram Panchayats (GPs) are connected as of May 2026. Through eGramSwaraj , over ₹3 lakh crore in payments have been processed, as of June 2026. O ver 1.28 lakh GPs are using SabhaSaar for creating meeting summaries, as of June 2026. Pathways to Prosperity: Livelihoods, Skills, and Financial Security Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) As of August 12, 2026, 10.19 crore households have been mobilised into 94.46 lakh SHGs. As of July 29, 2026, 3.46 crore Lakhpati Didis have been created. Role of Community Resource Persons in Ensuring Last-Mile Delivery of Schemes Over 9 lakh CRPs are currently active, serving thematic areas like agriculture, banking, insurance and nutrition. This includes more than 50,548 Bank Sakhis , 1.91 lakh Krishi Sakhis, 2,012 Matsya Sakhis, and 1.70 lakh Pashu Sakhis . Introduction of Self-Help Entrepreneur Mart (SHE-Mart) Announced in the Union Budget 2026-27, aiming to benefit 1 crore women . Aims to create community-owned retail spaces for women under the SHG ecosystem. Deendayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana Candidates trained increased from 43,038 in 2014–15 to 18.45 lakh till August 11, 2026. Candidates placed rose from 21,446 in 2014–15 to 12.35 lakh till August 11, 2026. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana Over 1.64 crore youth have received skill training since inception till June 2026. Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Total persondays generated between FY 2006-07 to FY 2013-14 were 1,660 crore, whereas, between FY 2014-15 to FY 2024-25, it rose to 3,029 crore. Women’s participation increased from 48% (FY 2013–14) to 58.19% (FY 2024–25). e-Shram Portal Registrations increased from 14.40 crore (Dec 2021) to 31.87 crore (August 12, 2026). PM Vishwakarma Yojana As of August 12, 2026, over 30 lakh traditional artisans have been registered . As of August 12, 2026, 24.32 lakh artisans have received skill training and 17.70 lakh have received toolkits. PM SVANidhi Number of beneficiaries has increased from 26.37 lakh (Nov 2021) to 78.17 lakh (August 12, 2026). As of August 12, 2026, loans amounting to ₹ 18,971.18 crore have been disbursed . 46% of the beneficiaries are women. PM MUDRA Yojana Total number of loans sanctioned have increased from 3.49 crore (2016) to over 59.14 crore (July 2026). PM Jan Dhan Yojana Number of beneficiaries have increased from 17.9 crore (Aug 2015) to 58.90 crore (August 12, 2026). Expanding Social Security Coverage Under National Pension System , beneficiaries increased from 1.05 crore (2016–17) to 2.17 crore (2025–26). Under Atal Pension Yojana , beneficiaries increased from 48.80 lakh (2016–17) to 9.29 crore (June 2026). 27.90 crore people covered by Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana up to July 2026. 58.78 crore people covered under Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana up to July 1, 2026. More than 54 lakh unorganised sector workers have been registered under Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan scheme as of July 2026. Accelerating Tribal Development through Integrated Interventions Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) As of August 5, 2026, 540 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVK) have been sanctioned, benefiting 46,042 persons from Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups . Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PM-JVM) 4,172 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras sanctioned, benefitting 12.48 lakh tribals under this scheme, as of August 2026. Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan (PM-JUGA) It combines the efforts of 17 ministries and focuses on filling long-standing gaps in tribal-majority villages and PVTG habitations. Under PM JUGA, the emphasis has increasingly moved from isolated interventions to coordinated, mission-mode delivery across sectors and ministries. In last 12 years- 7.60 lakh tribal houses have been completed and 28,303 tribal villages have access to drinking water . 59,812 tribal households and public institutions have been electrified and 657 Anganwadi Centres have been operationalized in tribal areas. 692 hostels have also sanctioned for tribal students. Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) As of August 12, 2026, over 4.16 lakh Scheduled Caste (SC) houses have been built, over 4.17 lakh SC households are covered under health protection schemes , and more than 3.57 lakh SC households have individual toilets. 17,578 villages have been declared Adarsh Grams as of August 12, 2026. Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs) Operational schools increased from 129 (2014–15) to 511 (August 12, 2026). As of August 12, 2026, EMRSs have an enrolment of 1.68 lakh students. PM-YASASVI 20.61 lakh students have received pre-matric scholarship, and 24.53 lakh students have received post-matric scholarship for FY 2024-25. Scholarships for Scheduled Tribe (ST) Students Between April 2024 and August 12, 2026, Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme has benefitted more than 28.99 lakh tribal students. National Fellowship for ST Students supported 2,961 research scholars in 2025–26. 56% of the beneficiaries were females. Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS) The Top-Class Education for SC Students scheme enabled 8,571 students to study in leading institutions such as IITs, IIMs, NITs and AIIMS in 2025-26. National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) 89,915 sewer and septic tank workers and more than 2.81 lakh waste pickers have been validated as of July 2026. Scheme for Economic Empowerment of De-Notified Tribes (SEED) During 2025-26, ₹26.75 crore was disbursed for the educational empowerment of 4,485 De-Notified Tribe (DNT) students . 73,569 Ayushman Bharat cards have been issued to DNT families, under the health component, during 2025-26. More than 54 lakh unorganised sector workers have been registered under Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan scheme as of July 2026. Accelerating Tribal Development through Integrated Interventions Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) As of August 5, 2026, 540 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVK) have been sanctioned, benefiting 46,042 persons from Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups . Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PM-JVM) 4,172 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras sanctioned, benefitting 12.48 lakh tribals under this scheme, as of August 2026. Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan (PM-JUGA) It combines the efforts of 17 ministries and focuses on filling long-standing gaps in tribal-majority villages and PVTG habitations. Under PM JUGA, the emphasis has increasingly moved from isolated interventions to coordinated, mission-mode delivery across sectors and ministries. In last 12 years- 7.60 lakh tribal houses have been completed and 28,303 tribal villages have access to drinking water . 59,812 tribal households and public institutions have been electrified and 657 Anganwadi Centres have been operationalized in tribal areas. 692 hostels have also sanctioned for tribal students. Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) As of August 12, 2026, over 4.16 lakh Scheduled Caste (SC) houses have been built, over 4.17 lakh SC households are covered under health protection schemes , and more than 3.57 lakh SC households have individual toilets. 17,578 villages have been declared Adarsh Grams as of August 12, 2026. Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs) Operational schools increased from 129 (2014–15) to 511 (August 12, 2026). As of August 12, 2026, EMRSs have an enrolment of 1.68 lakh students. PM-YASASVI 20.61 lakh students have received pre-matric scholarship, and 24.53 lakh students have received post-matric scholarship for FY 2024-25. Scholarships for Scheduled Tribe (ST) Students Between April 2024 and August 12, 2026, Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme has benefitted more than 28.99 lakh tribal students. National Fellowship for ST Students supported 2,961 research scholars in 2025–26. 56% of the beneficiaries were females. Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS) The Top-Class Education for SC Students scheme enabled 8,571 students to study in leading institutions such as IITs, IIMs, NITs and AIIMS in 2025-26. National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) 89,915 sewer and septic tank workers and more than 2.81 lakh waste pickers have been validated as of July 2026. Scheme for Economic Empowerment of De-Notified Tribes (SEED) During 2025-26, ₹26.75 crore was disbursed for the educational empowerment of 4,485 De-Notified Tribe (DNT) students . 73,569 Ayushman Bharat cards have been issued to DNT families, under the health component, during 2025-26.
